# Case and doors: the commands of the loop

Read for [`fgos-cook`](../SKILL.md). Case semantics (milestones, admission, frame,
refusals) are in `docs/platform/workflow/spec.md` and the shared doctrine
[`../../_shared/coordination-driver.md`](../../_shared/coordination-driver.md); this
file only fixes which command each step of this skill runs. Run every `fgos` command
with stdin closed (`</dev/null`).

## 1. One worktree and the case

`fgos workflow propose` prints, as its first two lines, the commands that create the
case's worktree and open the case; run them as printed, with the names and numbers it
chose (do not pick your own branch name or frame):

```sh
fgos worktree create <path> --branch <name> [--base <commit>]
fgos workflow start coding/feature --request "<outcome>" \
  --frame dispatches=<n>,mutatingDispatches=<n>,seatLaunchesPerDispatch=<n>,rigorFloor=<floor> \
  [--inherit <closedCaseId>] --worktree <path> --json
```

Slices run serially, so one linked worktree and one branch carry the whole case; the
runner commits each slice's declared `writes` onto it after a passing round.
`worktree create` provisions dependencies and the skill directories (so a worker that
declares `ak:cook` finds it). `workflow start` returns the `workflowRunId`, which is the
`caseId` every later line names. When a closed case with the same plan and base commit
is continued (`--inherit`), the proposal has no judge and validate lines: that case
already did them. The guide `coding/feature` has activities and no process: nothing
advances unless you run a line. Start only after the owner approved the frame. A frame
flag may narrow the guide's defaults, never widen them, so a widened frame later means
a new proposal and a question.

## 2. The rest of the printed lines

After the two lines above come, in order, the read passes, one `fgos run` per slice
(with any early or follow-up review), and a last `workflow gate`. Section 5 says what
each flag of a `fgos run` line means; they are printed, not composed.

## 3. Observe

```sh
fgos workflow status <caseId> --json     # read data.case
```

`data.case` gives milestones with digests (`achieved`, `stale`, `blocked`,
`unreached`), `eligible` activities, the listed routes and the unlisted path,
`frameRemaining`, open gates, live reservations, bindings and `closable`.

Guide activities for a plan: `judge-ambiguity` or `lock-decisions` (reach
`decisions-locked`), `validate-plan` (a reviewed read-only pass over the plan,
reaches `plan-validated`), `implement-item` (a writing slice, reviewed, reaches
`child-verified`), `review-item` (read-only; it needs only `plan-validated`, so it can
read work that is not yet verified), `fix-verify-red`, `scoped-subtask`,
`scout-blast-radius`, `resolve-question`, `integrate`. The decision points say which
route is `should` and which `may-instead`; going elsewhere is allowed with a reason.

## 4. Self-check of the case

After the first activity that passes (normally the first `validate-plan` or
`judge-ambiguity`), read `status` again. The milestone that activity produces must
now be `achieved`. If it is still `unreached` although the dispatch settled `pass`
or `findings`, the case is not recording progress: stop, do not dispatch another
slice, report `milestone-not-recorded` with the run ids and the status you read, as
a question for the owner. Do not work around it by running writes outside the case
(an unnamed run is uncounted and the case never sees it).

## 5. Dispatch a slice

First `fgos dispatch decide --for <capability>` (the answer tells you whether
anything serves it; `unavailable` is a blocker to ask about). Then run the slice's
printed `fgos run` line, replacing the case slot with the `caseId`. It always names
the case. The shape of such a line, for reading and for the rare change you must make
to one with a reason:

```sh
fgos run "<slice objective, with the plan phase and locked decisions it rests on>" \
  --case <caseId> --activity <activity> [--route should|may-instead|unlisted] [--reason "<text>"] \
  --capability <c> --rigor <r> \
  [--writes <paths> --worktree <path> --verify "<narrow pass/fail command>"] \
  [--input <plan.md>,<phase file>] \
  [--pattern <name>] [--params '<json object>'] [--param <key=value>] \
  [--persona <name>] [--timeout <dur>] --json
```

Changing the degree: the door inherits the activity's `unit`. Pass `--pattern`,
`--params` or repeatable `--param` only to change the degree for this dispatch.
A params request in a case and an explicit swap away from the activity's pattern
require `--reason` (`request-reason-required` otherwise); standalone params do not.
An identical explicit selector is not automatically a swap. Read the result's pin
for the effective pattern, loop, params and the request reason: it shows what ran
and why.

- A writing slice names the case worktree and a `--verify` command. `implement-item`
  inherits `reviewed`; `fix-verify-red` declares no unit, so it can run `solo`.
  A solo run with `--verify` verifies once and can leave a receipt; without a
  command it leaves none, which the milestone then shows. A reviewed run without
  a verify command also verifies nothing. When driving from an installed release
  older than this branch, still pass `--pattern reviewed` by hand with a verify
  command, because an older solo run does not verify.
- Writes are exactly the files the slice may change after the expansion `propose`
  showed; a path the worker needs outside them comes back as `needsWrites`,
  and you decide whether to widen this slice or add another.
- Several independent read-only checks may go as one bounded wave nested in the
  case: `fgos workflow start --units <file> --case <caseId>` (charged to the frame
  first). Never a wave of writers.
- A slice to be done with `ak:cook` goes through `--unit <file>` with
  `skills: ["ak:cook"]`, and its objective carries the brief of
  [`cook-worker-contract.md`](../../_shared/cook-worker-contract.md). The
  Unit names only the skill; `bind()` still picks the executor.
- Read `--json`: `data.results[-1].runResult.agentClaim.summary` and
  `data.results[-1].commit`. The outcome is one of `pass`, `findings`,
  `execution-failure`, `policy-refusal`, `provider-limit`, `blocked`.

A refused dispatch prints a code and a condition (`entry-milestone-unmet`,
`writes-overlap`, `frame-exhausted`, `seat-launch-ceiling`, `consent-missing` ...).
Re-read `status`, change the proposal or stop; do not repeat it.

## 6. Verify it yourself

After every writing slice, in the case worktree:

1. re-run the slice's own verify command;
2. `git -C <path> diff --stat <before>..HEAD` and compare the paths with the declared
   writes (anything else is a finding against the slice);
3. read the checker report under `.fgos/assignments/<unitRunId>/`.

Record `slice, activity, run id, outcome, what you re-ran, result` in the notebook.

## 7. Findings and adaptation

For each finding: accepted (dispatch `fix-verify-red` or a fix slice, then an
independent recheck by another slice or the next reviewed round), rejected (reason
in the notebook), deferred (only outside the approved scope). A finding is never
discharged by your word alone. Bounds per slice: the pattern's rounds, then one fix
slice, one read-only diagnosis (`code:debug`), one rigor raise; then park a question.

## 8. Questions

Park each owner question in the notebook with its five parts
(`../../_shared/decision-question.md`). Ask when nothing else can progress, or at the
frame's checkpoints, all together. Slices independent of a parked question go on.

## 9. Integrate and hand off

All slices are on the case branch, so there is nothing to merge. The proposal's last
line is `fgos workflow gate <caseId> --worktree <path> --writes <paths> --capability code:implement`: run it as
printed. The runner, not a seat, runs the whole-worktree check in the case worktree and
settles the receipt of the integrated tree; only a passing gate reaches `integrated`.
Run the plan's own full verification in the worktree yourself as well when it is wider
than the gate's command (use a long `--timeout` or run it directly; a short limit reads
as a failure). Then report: branch and commits, evidence you ran, plan vs built, parked
questions, frame used vs approved. Do not edit plan status, do not write consent, do not
merge. Leave the case open until the owner decides; `fgos workflow close <caseId>`
follows their decision.

## 10. Notebook

One file per case, outside the case worktree (a write there would dirty the tree a
round reads). Name it with `fgos convention path --kind report --type cook-notebook --slug <plan-slug>`.
Keep it short: caseId, branch, worktree, approved frame, slice list with state, the
rows from section 6, dispositions, parked questions, deferred items. The case ledger
is the truth; the notebook is for cold resume. Commit it only with an explicit
pathspec when the repository's practice allows, otherwise leave it and name its path
in the report.
